summary:
Deltawatch is an interactive, browser-native mission control dashboard engineered to make complex NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) data accessible and actionable for disaster response.
We built this to solve a critical bottleneck: local responders and citizens in vulnerable coastal deltas and floodplains (like Nagapattinam and Majuli) often lack the technical expertise or bandwidth to process raw HDF5 radar files during an emergency. Deltawatch bridges this gap by wrapping heavy aerospace physics—like L-Band cloud penetration and volumetric SRTM depth modeling—into an intuitive, "Apple Maps-style" interface.
Users can seamlessly swipe between pre-event baselines and post-event inundation, filter 6 distinct classes of backscatter physics (e.g., distinguishing open water from flooded crop canopy), and correlate radar detections with live NASA POWER river discharge telemetry. By integrating a Gemini 2.5 Flash query engine directly into the browser, Deltawatch empowers anyone to instantly generate grounded, location-specific scientific impact briefings and evacuation protocols without needing a PhD in remote sensing.
details:
Github link : https://github.com/mehulraikwar07/deltawatch.git

Deltawatch ingests processed NISAR L-Band (24 cm) radar composites and renders them into a highly interactive, 3D topographical web application. We utilized MapLibre's WebGL engine to drape extreme-exaggeration SRTM elevation meshes and volumetric flood extrusions under a consumer-grade glassmorphic UI. The platform operates on a split-screen paradigm: the left side displays dry pre-event backscatter, while the right side renders the post-event flood mask colored by scattering mechanisms (specular vs. dihedral double-bounce). An integrated AI sidebar parses this spatial data against live Open-Meteo and NASA POWER hydrological APIs to generate real-time, localized science reports.

The core benefit is democratization of Earth observation data. By abstracting the heavy lifting of GIS software (like ArcScene) and delivering a zero-latency, 60fps web experience, Deltawatch allows disaster management agencies, local governments, and even farmers to monitor crop inundation timelines, track levee breaches, and export emergency GeoJSON polygons directly from their phones or laptops.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used:

Frontend Framework: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS

Geospatial Engine: MapLibre GL JS, AWS Terrarium DEM (SRTM)

Data Sources: NASA GIBS (IMERG Rainfall), NASA POWER API (Temperature/Precipitation), Open-Meteo (River Discharge)

Github link : https://github.com/mehulraikwar07/deltawatch.git
